The EU Digital Product Passport registry is already live. The next mandatory deadline — DPPs for EV, industrial and LMT batteries — is about six months out, and the products that fall under it will need a working data trail in place before that date, not after.

AuthiChain generates and anchors that data trail — from raw material sourcing to point of sale — using signed QR codes and on-chain anchoring, so a product's provenance record travels with it instead of living in a spreadsheet somewhere else.

Each unit gets a cryptographically signed QR code. Scanning it surfaces the product's passport: origin, custody events, and certifications tied to that SKU. The underlying record is anchored to a public ledger, so the passport history can't be quietly edited after the fact.

If your product falls under an upcoming DPP deadline and you want to see how a signed passport works end to end before it's due, take a look.

reddit.title: The EU DPP battery deadline is about six months out — how are you handling the passport data trail?
reddit.body:
The EU DPP registry went live this summer, and the first mandatory deadline — DPPs for EV, industrial and LMT batteries — is about six months out. I've been working on AuthiChain, a system for generating signed QR-based product passports and anchoring the provenance record each one points to, so the history can't be silently rewritten after the fact. It's aimed at brands that need to trace a product's history — origin, custody, certifications — from raw material to shelf, ahead of that deadline.

Curious how others here are approaching the technical side: building the passport layer in-house, using a vendor's DPP platform, or bolting a QR code onto an existing ERP? What's been the hardest part — the data model, the QR issuance side, or getting suppliers to actually submit clean data?

Disclosure: I work on this project.
